Definition: from G473 and G1303; to set oneself opposite, i.e. be disputatious:--that oppose themselves.
BiblicalUsage: In his charge to Timothy, Paul says the servant of the Lord must be gentle, able to teach those who oppose themselves, if God will give them repentance. The word names the disputatious, the ones set against the truth.
TheologicalSignificance: A single word for the disputatious carries no doctrine of its own; its hope is Paul's, that even those who oppose themselves may yet be given repentance.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
